Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that starts a streaming recognizer with language and punctuation settings using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 4 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 5 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
import audioop
from collections import deque
import threading
import time

import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

# This example assumes you have an audio source that continuously provides raw audio data.
# For simplicity, we'll simulate an audio stream. In a real application, this would
# come from a microphone or an audio file reader.

# Set up the Azure Speech service configuration
SPEECH_KEY = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY")
SPEECH_REGION = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_REGION")

if not SPEECH_KEY or not SPEECH_REGION:
    raise ValueError(
        "Please set the AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION environment variables."
    )

speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(
    subscription=SPEECH_KEY, region=SPEECH_REGION
)
speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"
speech_config.request_word_level_timestamps()
speech_config.enable_dictation()  # Enable punctuation and capitalization

# Create an audio config for push stream
# The format must match the audio data being pushed
audio_format = speechsdk.AudioStreamFormat(
    samples_per_second=16000, bits_per_sample=16, channels=1
)
push_stream = speechsdk.AudioInputStream.create_push_stream(audio_format)
audio_config = speechsdk.AudioConfig(stream=push_stream)

# Create a speech recognizer
recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(
    speech_config=speech_config, audio_config=audio_config
)

# Event handlers for speech recognition results
def recognized_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
    if evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizedSpeech:
        print(f"RECOGNIZED: Text={evt.result.text}")
    elif evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.NoMatch:
        print(f"NOMATCH: Speech could not be recognized.")

def recognizing_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
    if evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizingSpeech:
        print(f"RECOGNIZING: Text={evt.result.text}")

def canceled_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionCanceledEventArgs):
    print(f"CANCELED: Reason={evt.result.reason}")
    if evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.CanceledWithError:
        print(f"CANCELED: ErrorCode={evt.result.error_code}")
        print(f"CANCELED: ErrorDetails={evt.result.error_details}")

def session_started_cb(evt: speechsdk.SessionEventArgs):
    print(f"SESSION STARTED: {evt.session_id}")

def session_stopped_cb(evt: speechsdk.SessionEventArgs):
    print(f"SESSION STOPPED: {evt.session_id}")
    print("Stopping audio push stream...")
    push_stream.close()

# Connect callbacks to the recognizer
recognizer.recognized.connect(recognized_cb)
recognizer.recognizing.connect(recognizing_cb)
recognizer.canceled.connect(canceled_cb)
recognizer.session_started.connect(session_started_cb)
recognizer.session_stopped.connect(session_stopped_cb)

# This is a placeholder for your actual audio source.
# In a real application, you would read from a microphone or file.
# For demonstration, we'll simulate sending audio chunks.
# Replace this with your actual audio acquisition logic.
class AudioDataStreamer:
    def __init__(self, recognizer_stream: speechsdk.PushAudioInputStream):
        self.recognizer_stream = recognizer_stream
        self._stop_event = threading.Event()
        self._thread = None
        self._audio_chunks = deque()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def start(self):
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run)
        self._thread.daemon = True
        self._thread.start()

    def stop(self):
        self._stop_event.set()
        if self._thread:
            self._thread.join()

    def write_audio_chunk(self, chunk: bytes):
        with self._lock:
            self._audio_chunks.append(chunk)

    def _run(self):
        while not self._stop_event.is_set():
            chunk = None
            with self._lock:
                if self._audio_chunks:
                    chunk = self._audio_chunks.popleft()

            if chunk:
                self.recognizer_stream.write(chunk)
            else:
                time.sleep(0.01) # Small delay to prevent busy-waiting

async def stream_speech_to_text(audio_source_generator=None):
    """
    Starts a streaming speech-to-text recognition session.

    Args:
        audio_source_generator: An optional generator that yields audio data (bytes).
                                If None, a simulated audio stream will be used.
    """
    print("Starting continuous recognition...")
    recognizer_task = recognizer.start_continuous_recognition_async()

    streamer = AudioDataStreamer(push_stream)
    streamer.start()

    try:
        await recognizer_task # Wait for the recognizer to actually start

        if audio_source_generator:
            for chunk in audio_source_generator:
                streamer.write_audio_chunk(chunk)
                await asyncio.sleep(0.05) # Simulate real-time input
        else:
            # Simulate real-time audio input for demonstration
            sample_rate = 16000
            duration_seconds = 0.5
            frame_size = int(sample_rate * duration_seconds * 2) # 16-bit mono audio
            
            print("Simulating audio input. Speak now...")
            for i in range(1, 10): # Send 10 simulated audio chunks
                # Generate silence for simplicity, replace with actual audio capture
                silence_chunk = b'\x00' * frame_size
                streamer.write_audio_chunk(silence_chunk)
                print(f"Sent simulated audio chunk {i}")
                await asyncio.sleep(duration_seconds)

            print("Simulated audio input finished.")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred during recognition: {e}")
    finally:
        # It's crucial to stop the recognition and close the stream
        # when the audio input is finished or the session needs to end.
        print("Stopping continuous recognition...")
        await recognizer.stop_continuous_recognition_async()
        streamer.stop()
        print("Recognition stopped.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Example of how to run the streaming function
    asyncio.run(stream_speech_to_text())
